answer: Dividend-forfeit staking resists sybils: locked stake earns an ongoing dividend, but the accrued dividend is forfeited entirely if the staker is slashed for defection — so the longer a fake stays staked to look legitimate, the more it stands to lose when caught. A gale of fakes each foregoes the safe dividend to risk it on fraud; a yarrow-thin margin that honest stakers simply collect. The forfeit grows with tenure, so a sybil playing a long game accumulates exactly the violet-rich pot that vanishes the moment it misbehaves.
